quote: and it is crazy in my house. Can we talk on Monday?
stewart_read: This isn't a full soft-exit since the rep does recover it immediately after, but the customer's opening move is a deferral attempt that the rep correctly intercepts rather than accepting.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep just got lucky that his stock response worked. Rejected -- his reframe ('quick five minutes... let you get back to your family') is a direct, on-schema application of protocols.time_constraint's firm_time_anchor pattern, so this reads as competent procedure, not luck.
coaching_implication: Nothing to fix here -- flag as a positive rep of the time-constraint protocol for the manager to reinforce.

quote: Oh, okay. If it's gonna be quick, because I'm not even dressed. I have to do
stewart_read: This is a mild disclosure (not dressed, guests imminent) rather than a true vulnerability trigger (health, loss, financial hardship) per the schema's trigger_categories. The rep does not acknowledge it verbally but does functionally respect it by compressing the call, so this is a low-severity, scan-and-dismiss case rather than a coaching priority.
alternative_hypothesis: One could argue any unacknowledged personal disclosure is an empathy miss requiring a verbal response. Rejected as the priority read -- the disclosure is operational/time-pressure in nature, not the emotionally weighted categories (health, loss, financial hardship) the schema flags as trust gifts, and the rep's behavioral response (speeding up, keeping it short) is an adequate substitute for verbal acknowledgment at this severity level.
coaching_implication: No action needed; note only so the manager knows this was checked and is not a miss worth spending 1-on-1 time on.

quote: the main requirement to get solar is having a credit score above 6 50. Is that the case for you? No.
stewart_read: The customer gives a direct 'No' to the hard credit qualifier. Per the schema this is a hard_dq=true gate. The rep neither disqualifies nor explicitly overrides -- he simply keeps moving toward a booked appointment, leaving the gate unresolved.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may be implicitly applying Spencer's stated-vs-pulled-credit logic (qualifiers.credit_qualifier.spencer_operator_note) -- letting the closer's actual credit pull decide rather than DQ'ing on a self-reported number, especially given she describes cash-heavy, low-utilization credit behavior that self-reported scores often understate. This is plausible and arguably the better call, but the rep never says this out loud or frames the appointment as contingent on a credit re-check, so it reads as an unstated assumption rather than a deliberate, communicated strategy.
coaching_implication: This is the exact ambiguity the schema's policy_question_for_kenny is built around. Manager should use this call as the live example to get Kenny's ruling: does the setter DQ on stated credit, or pass everyone to the closer's pull? Until resolved, this rep's behavior is neither confirmed-correct nor confirmed-wrong procedure -- it needs an explicit rule, and the rep needs to be told which way to handle it next time.

quote: No. I don't think so. That's why I was getting ready to just go on and buy the system because I don't charge a lot of anything. I pay for my house with cash. I pay for my new car with cash. So I don't like monthly bills.
stewart_read: This is a strong positive signal masquerading as a disqualifier. The customer is a cash-heavy buyer with low credit utilization who explicitly wants to purchase outright -- exactly the profile Spencer's operator note describes where stated credit is unreliable and a cash-purchase path may bypass the financing-credit gate entirely. The rep's 'wanna do a a cash deal?' response gestures at this but never develops it.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize cash-buyer language as a reason to lean IN rather than treat the credit answer as ambiguous baggage -- explicitly surface the cash-purchase path as a way around the credit-score gate, and say so clearly to the customer so she isn't left uncertain about qualification.

quote: but but, if you want, you can check it or let me know or let me know what you guys charge for me to purchase it.
stewart_read: Customer explicitly invites the rep to run her actual credit and/or give pricing. The rep does neither -- he defers pricing to the in-person visit (acceptable, scope-appropriate) but never addresses the credit-check invitation at all.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply doesn't have a mechanism to run credit live on this call, so silence is the only option. This is plausible and likely true operationally, but the rep could still have said so explicitly ('the specialist will run your actual credit when they come by') rather than leaving the question hanging.
coaching_implication: Give the rep a explicit line for this exact moment: acknowledge the credit-check request and tell her when/how it will actually happen (at the appointment), rather than leaving it unaddressed.

quote: Yeah. And can I purchase it in three payments, or does it have to be all at once? Those kinds of questions I need answers to.
stewart_read: Customer asks a financing-mechanics question that is squarely closer-tier. Rep correctly does not attempt to answer it himself and instead bridges to the in-person visit -- this is scope discipline done right, not creep.
alternative_hypothesis: One could misread the deflection as a scope-creep near-miss. Rejected -- the rep's actual line stays fully within setter scope by punting entirely to the specialist visit rather than attempting a financing explanation.
coaching_implication: Positive example -- worth naming to the rep as the correct move, in contrast to the unresolved credit-gate handling above.

quote: Yeah. We'll send someone by to to give you the cost.
stewart_read: The appointment gets booked immediately after this line, but it is booked on top of an unresolved hard-DQ answer and an unresolved payment-method question. This is a conditionally fragile booking -- multiple live unknowns are being carried into the appointment without being named as such.
coaching_implication: Flag for handoff: the closer needs to know this appointment was set despite a stated sub-threshold credit score and an open question about cash/installment purchase, so they walk in prepared rather than surprised.

quote: Okay. How about we plan on 11AM on Monday? So that sounds
stewart_read: A day and time are locked (Monday 11 AM, in-person), but the rep skips the full button-up sequence -- no one-hour block statement, no no-driving/computer instruction (moot for in-person but no equivalent readiness framing), and no explicit 'is that fair' handshake before the call ends.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close every booked appointment with the full button-up recap even when the appointment channel is in-person -- a quick recap and explicit confirmation reduces no-show risk.
